message:
My light touch signal clears the converter, where CDC means Capacitance-to-Digital Converter and LSB means Least Significant Bit step. Plain words: the tiny squeeze makes a few femtofarads that a normal touch chip can see. I take up the AD7147A (Rev. B) (E41) from Dr. Marcus Reid which states femtofarad resolution on 13 inputs, the How to adjust the sensitivity and calculate capacitance for AD7147 (E57) which states the input range is fixed at plus-minus 8 pF with 16-bit resolution so each count weighs 244 aF, and the How cheap digital verniers work (E56) which states the AD7147 has sub-femtofarad output noise. The numbers that decide it are 0.269 pF base in the base capacitance 1.5mm taxel 200um gap (E26) with 3.57 fF change in the check deltaC fF from base pF times strain (E55) giving 14.6 steps in the signal margin in LSB counts vs 244 aF LSB (E62), a whisper above room noise for Dr. Amara Okafor and Dr. Marcus Reid.

The same soft taxel does not bottom out at full grip, where PVDF means Polyvinylidene Fluoride vibration film. Plain words: pressure grows slowly with grip force so light touch and crushing grip fit in one squeeze. The High-Sensitive Wearable Capacitive Pressure Sensor with Hemispherical Porous Electrode--Institute of Semiconductors (E59) maintains sensitivity in 0 to 10 kPa, 10 to 100 kPa and 100 to 400 kPa ranges, and the A flexible capacitive pressure sensor with a hybrid porous PDMS/SA hydrogel structure for touch/pain detection (E58) keeps maximum sensitivity up to 400 kPa. The numbers that decide it are 5.78 kPa at 0.001 N rising to 213 kPa at 50 N with strain 1.33% to 48.9% in the dual-range strain sweep 1mN to 50N grip without saturation (E64), so 2 N grip is about 72.8 kPa and 16.7% squeeze for Dr. Elena Vasquez and Dr. Marcus Reid.

Curvature without crosstalk uses a compound-eye drape for Dr. Amara Okafor skin. Plain words: flat sensor tiles sit on flat facets around the curve while one continuous soft skin drapes over them like a cornea, keeping lithography flat and touch smooth. The Free and Forced Vibration Modes of the Human Fingertip (E60) gives fingertip width 18.0 mm and length 28.0 mm as finger scale. The numbers that decide it are 2.00 mm pitch sharing the 0.470 mm spot in the Hertz contact radius for 1mN on soft silicone (E14), held in the Faceted rigid core with flat flex tiles draped by continuous silicone skin like cornea over compound eye (E65). Not ready, because 2200 Hz PVDF sampling load and flex crosstalk under vibration still need the timed bench test with Dr. Elena Vasquez and Dr. Marcus Reid.
